verses.1: The LORD is king, robed with majesty; the LORD is robed, girded with might. The world will surely stand in place, never to be moved.
verses.2: Your throne stands firm from of old; you are from everlasting, LORD.
verses.3: The flood has raised up, LORD; the flood has raised up its roar; the flood has raised its pounding waves.
verses.4: More powerful than the roar of many waters, more powerful than the breakers of the sea, powerful in the heavens is the LORD.
verses.5: Your decrees are firmly established; holiness belongs to your house, LORD, for all the length of days.

notes.text: The LORD is king: literally, "the LORD reigns." This psalm, and Psalms 47; 96-99, are sometimes called enthronement psalms. They may have been used in a special liturgy during which God's ascent to the throne was ritually reenacted. They have also been interpreted eschatologically, pointing to the coming of God as king at the end-time.
The flood: the primordial sea was tamed by God in the act of creation. It is a figure of chaos and rebellion. Cf Psalm 46:4.
